classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied circle scaffolds and Pythagoras’ theorem, then select both possible signs.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Let $\sin\theta=-\frac{\sqrt7}{4}$.

Find the two possible values of $\cos\theta$.

spec.description: Coordinate circle with terminal rays in quadrants III and IV, paired right-angle marks, both hypotenuses labelled 4 and curved leaders identifying both vertical components as negative square root of 7. Horizontal components remain unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Radius 4; y=-sqrt(7); the two horizontal components are opposite in sign.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied scaffold marks and labels remain visible; unknown horizontal values are omitted.

answer.worked:
Using the right-angled triangles,
$$\begin{aligned}
|x|&=\sqrt{4^2-(\sqrt7)^2}\\
&=\sqrt{16-7}\\
&=3.
\end{aligned}$$
Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV. Cosine is negative in quadrant III and positive in quadrant IV.
$$\cos\theta=-\frac34\text{ or }\frac34.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Let $\cos\theta=-\frac14$.

Find the two possible values of $\sin\theta$.

spec.description: Coordinate circle with narrow triangles in quadrants II and III, terminal rays labelled theta, both right angles marked, curved leaders labelling both hypotenuses 4 and the shared horizontal component negative 1. Vertical components remain unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Radius 4; x=-1; the two vertical components are opposite in sign.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied scaffold marks and labels remain visible; unknown vertical values are omitted.

answer.worked:
Using the right-angled triangles,
$$\begin{aligned}
|y|&=\sqrt{4^2-1^2}\\
&=\sqrt{16-1}\\
&=\sqrt{15}.
\end{aligned}$$
Cosine is negative in quadrants II and III. Sine is positive in quadrant II and negative in quadrant III.
$$\sin\theta=\frac{\sqrt{15}}4\text{ or }-\frac{\sqrt{15}}4.$$
